Method of Attack: Phishing emails with lures pretending to be job application offers or copyright infringement notices
Downloading obfuscated PowerShell scripts or executables to encrypt files
System reconnaissance, data exfiltration, and payload loading
Use of VBA macros inside Word or DOTM documents to execute payloads
Disguising malicious executables as Word files to trick users into execution
Connecting to C2 servers to receive commands and download ransomware payloads
Dropping NSIS installers via fake copyright infringement emails
Impacted Systems: Windows systems running PowerShell and capable of executing VBA macros
Attack Vector: Phishing emails with malicious attachments (Word documents with macros, disguised executables)
Execution of VBA macros after user enables content
Indicators of Compromise: Use of LNK downloader file skem.lnk
Emails with attachments named Resume.exe or Word documents with macros
Ransom notes generated by LockBit encrypting user files
